questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country, far away, friendly people

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was more expensive than I'd imagined and I lost 6.000 kr on mandatory health insurance that I didn't need because I'm danish. I was supposed to receive a RAMQ card to redeem my money but it never arrived because they were "delayed"

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fine

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a Frosh thing that I took part in but the info on this wasn't good meaning that they didn't include what we were going to do. Fx I thought we were going on the trip as a big group but instead, we split into only being 7 people which is a bit disappointing, I would recommend going to the faculty frosh instead of the outdoor frosh.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: it was there if you wanted some help

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just applied via my university but there was no information in regard to the price and I first received my contract with the price a couple of days before I got there so I couldn't really say no. The housing was really expensive - 6.700 kr to live 10 min away from campus in public transportation in an non-soundproof apartment shared with 2 others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend finding somewhere to live on your own - so not through the host university. I got the impression that the Plateau area is a good place to live and is close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you get housing through the host university then you have to pay for a mandatory meal plan which is 7000 kr and they are not redeemable! The food they offer isn't that great and it's very overpriced.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went on their webside called Minerva

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: d

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I recommend starting to apply for your courses really early because it is first come first served. I had trouble tryingto find available courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: idk

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I choose some difficult courses but they were good

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two courses at 300 level which is corresponding to my level but one of them was a 300 course in virology which was stupid of me because I've never had any micro-biology beforehand in my BA so it was way to difficult for me. Other than that I had two 500 courses which is MA (I didn't know) but they were okay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Human Cognition and the Brain (300), Fundamental Virology (300), AI in Medicine (500), Economic Evaluation of Health Care Programs (500).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Human Cognition and the Brain - It was a bit hard but very interesting. Economic Evaluation of Health Care Programs - it was very relevant to my program and very interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had very good clubs, sports, etc. at the university - They had a whole building dedicated only to clubs and a huge stadium with a pool and fitness stuff - way better than at UCPH.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of different activities. I was a part of the knitting/crocheting club but there were also a bunch of other cultural, athletic, and social activities. You won't be disappointed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A social or athletic club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking or up the mountain to look at the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy - they're canadian/french here so it's more european than the US for example.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No, I didn't really get to socialize with them but that's on me because I kept to the other Danes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
For me, it was just easier to talk to the other Danes because we had more in common thus we had more to talk about. I think Danes are also more mature than Canadians because we started uni at 20 whereas they start uni at 17.
Another challenging cultural difference was the amount of homeless people - they had a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There were a surprising amount of exchange students and generally just a lot of different cultures in Montreal which was nice because everyone was speaking in an accent so it didn't stand out that I/we also were speaking in an accent.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not live in housing through the university, be a part of a club, and do either the outdoor camping frosh or the faculty frosh.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to do the RAMQ application correctly because you only get one chance as they are extremely delayed. I've waited almost 4 months now but it might be because there was an error in the application but others also waited 3 months before they received theirs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Now I've seen Canada

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: School and making friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
